topics.topic: Whether and how bubblewrap must preserve the trap-channel file descriptors for the child runner
questions: These cannot both govern the implementation: subprocess pass_fds preserves descriptors only through exec of bubblewrap, while bubblewrap closes additional descriptors unless its existing --preserve-fds option is used. Must --preserve-fds be allowed, or must another specified mechanism carry the trap channel to the runner?
Which passage must change: must bubblewrap preserve the inherited descriptors for the child, or is descriptor preservation unavailable?

quotes: Every descriptor the environment needs from the parent — the write end of the trap channel, the --info-fd pipe — reaches bubblewrap by inheritance, passed with subprocess pass_fds, and bubblewrap keeps it open for the child: bubblewrap has no option that names a descriptor to keep, and --preserve-fds does not exist.
judgement.why: This is the same question about preserving the trap-channel descriptors for the runner that P1 already judged answered, and the quoted passage has not changed.

precedent.topic: Whether bubblewrap must preserve and pass the execute_function trap-channel descriptors to the sandbox child
quotes: Every descriptor the environment needs from the parent — the write end of the trap channel, the --info-fd pipe — reaches bubblewrap by inheritance, passed with subprocess pass_fds, and bubblewrap keeps it open for the child: bubblewrap has no option that names a descriptor to keep, and --preserve-fds does not exist.
precedent.why: The text explicitly requires pass_fds inheritance into bubblewrap and requires bubblewrap to keep the descriptors open for its child.

topics.topic: When a non-empty mapped output must be written relative to fit checking and successful delivery
questions: Must a non-empty mapped output be written before its fit check even when that check fails and the value is never delivered, or only when it is first successfully delivered?

quotes: published with put_value_bytes and written by runs when the list is first delivered, never in an element's own change — except the empty list, which the node's one NodeExecution over an empty list names and writes (A13 rule 6)

Every StoredValue runs derives for delivery and no NodeExecution names — the list element a mapped element receives, and a non-empty mapped node's value output (the array of its elements' values) when first delivered — MUST be written with record_change in a RecordRunProgressChange with no executions, status running and the run's waiting points and outputs unchanged before fit_port_value checks it and before execute_function_element or reach_operation_element receives it: read_value_bytes, and every module below runs, reads only a StoredValue that is written.
judgement.why: The first passage conditions writing on the list being delivered, while the second requires writing before the fit check that can reject it and prevent delivery.
